messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 2026-03-14T18:20Z - ALERT: Elevated BGP withdrawals and VPN packet loss reported from Azure France Central (francecentral). Potential impact: site-to-site VPN / partner interconnect customers and Private deployments with on-prem tunnels. Paging @oncall-sre :rotating_light:

oncall-sre: Acknowledged. I'm looking at BGP telemetry now. Confirming increased update rate across multiple VPN gateways.

maria_gonzalez: Which customer environments are we seeing this in? Any Dedicated pools or Private control planes impacted?

support-ops: Quick list from observability (cropped):
- cust-842 (Private VPC via partner VPN) - packet loss 8-25%
- cust-199 (Dedicated, cross-region replication failing) - TCP timeouts
- cust-710 (on-prem SAP integration) - intermittent disconnects
We have multiple support tickets opened.

samir_kapoor: Posting BGP/route snapshot from our collector (prefixes anonymized):
```
Timestamp: 2026-03-14T18:21:03Z
FR-VCG-01 -> updates: 214 withdrawals / min
BGP: 64592 withdrawn prefixes, 128 flapping sessions
Routes showing high MED/AS_PATH churn for 203.0.113.0/24 and 198.51.100.0/24
```
Also seeing traceroute from cust-842 to our private gateway: 
```
traceroute to 10.20.0.1 (10.20.0.1), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.240.1.1  1.23 ms  1.14 ms  1.09 ms
 2  100.64.5.1  12.6 ms  12.8 ms !H  12.9 ms
 3  * * *
```
Packets consistently dropping at Azure gateway hop.

ira_devops: Possible mitigation paths: 1) Add temporary static routes/blackhole for extremely noisy prefixes per-customer, 2) Reroute customer traffic via west europe regional peering (westeurope) using our smart routing, 3) Ask customers to fail traffic to Dedicated pools in other regions.

oncall-sre: I'll start option 2 and prepare per-customer routing rules. Samir, can you open a support escalation with Azure (severity A) and share the SR id here?

samir_kapoor: Opening now, SR created: SR# 20260314-AC-7782. Azure-support-bot: "SR 20260314-AC-7782 - Acknowledged. Engaging FR-C NOC. Confirmed elevated VPN gateway CPU and control-plane restarts."

support-ops: Drafting customer notices. Minimal wording for API/webhooks: "We are investigating intermittent connectivity to services in Azure France Central that may impact private/on-prem integrations. Our engineers are actively mitigating and we will share updates every 30 minutes." Anyone want to add impact specifics?

maria_gonzalez: Please call out that Dedicated ingestion pipelines may have delayed writes and that we expect increased latencies for embeddings created in FR-C.

chris_prod: Noted. I'll push a banner and update status.redwood.ai. Use INCIDENT-20260314-FR-C as public ref.

oncall-sre: Executing reroute to westeurope for cust-842 and cust-710 now. Applying temporary prefix policy (examples):
```
route-map RM-TEMP permit 10
 set as-path prepend 65001 65001
 set local-preference 200
```
Applied. Monitoring logs.

support-ops: Customers cust-842 and cust-710 have been notified (email + support portal). Reaction: :thumbsup:.

samir_kapoor: Azure NOC responded: "We are seeing a hardware fault on a subset of VPN gateway fabric in francecentral. Hotfix deployment in progress; estimated mitigation 45-60 minutes." They asked us not to make mass BGP flaps while they patch.

oncall-sre: Aware. I've paused any aggressive withdrawals and kept static reroutes in place. Rolling monitoring shows packet loss dropping from 20% -> 4% for cust-842 over 12 minutes.

ira_devops: For Dedicated customers we also enabled TCP retry/backoff on the replication workers to reduce error storms. Config snippet applied: `REPLICA_BACKOFF_MS=1200`

support-ops: Handoff note: @oncall-sre will stay primary until 19:15Z, then hand off to @samir_kapoor for overnight watch. Will update the on-call bot.

oncall-sre: Handoff: leaving a summary for night shift: "FR-C VPN fabric instability; Azure SR 20260314-AC-7782; temporary reroute to westeurope for critical customers; static route policies in place; customer notifications sent; monitoring channel = this thread. Escalate to SRE lead if packet loss > 10% for 3 consecutive windows."

support-ops: Customers reporting intermittent improvements. We'll keep PD (priority) tickets open.

azure-support-bot: Update on SR 20260314-AC-7782: Hotfix applied to affected VPN blades at 2026-03-14T18:48Z. Control-plane restarts completed. NOC monitoring for stability.

oncall-sre: Confirming - we see BGP update rate returning to baseline and packet loss under 1% for most impacted prefixes. Leaving reroute rules for 30 minutes to ensure convergence, then will gracefully remove them.

chris_prod: I've pushed a status update: "Mitigation in progress - Azure reports control-plane fix; we are monitoring and will confirm resolution soon."

support-ops: Sending final customer note template: "Update: Azure reports applied hotfix to VPN gateways in France Central. We've applied temporary routing mitigations; most customers are seeing restored connectivity. We will follow up with a detailed incident report."

oncall-sre: Rolling back temporary routing rules now (graceful withdraw).

samir_kapoor: Confirming rollback completed at 2026-03-14T19:10Z. BGP sessions stable. No further control-plane restarts observed.

incident-bot: INCIDENT 2026-03-14T19:23Z - RESOLVED: Azure France Central VPN fabric instability - degrade -> resolved. Postmortem scheduled in #postmortems in 48h. Refer to INCIDENT-20260314-FR-C.

maria_gonzalez: Thanks team. Action items for postmortem: 1) evaluate whether automatic failover to regional peering should be faster for Private tenants, 2) retry/backoff defaults for Dedicated replication, 3) add Azure VPN appliance health metrics to our alerting to detect control-plane restarts earlier.

support-ops: Filing follow-up tickets and assigned owners in the incident doc.

oncall-sre: Handoff complete to @samir_kapoor. I'll be available if anything regress. Good job everyone. :tada:
